cases.summary: Reset clears the write pointer and read data but not the read pointer.
A write while full is accepted when a read arrives in the same cycle.
The write pointer's wrap bit never toggles.
A read while empty is not ignored and advances the read pointer.
A simultaneous read and write increments the occupancy count.
empty stays asserted while one word is stored.
Reset does not win over a simultaneous write.
Writes go to bit-reversed slots, so reads return words out of order.

briefs.text: An 8-entry, 8-bit synchronous FIFO for buffering ADC samples. Writes when full are dropped and reads when empty are ignored.
A 4-entry log buffer. When it is full, a new write should replace the oldest byte so the most recent bytes are always kept.
A 2-entry FIFO. When it is empty and a byte is written while a read is requested, the read should return that same byte immediately so data passes straight through.
A 4-deep FIFO carrying 16-bit audio samples from an I2S receiver to a DSP block, with synchronous reset.
A depth-2 handshake buffer between a parser and an ALU, 8-bit data, with a synchronous reset that may be asserted at any time to flush it.
A 4-byte FIFO for an SPI transmitter. Software may try to push when it is full; those pushes are lost. Pops when it is empty do nothing.
A small 4-deep byte queue. If a push and a pop happen in the same cycle while it is partially full, both take effect and the number of stored bytes stays the same.
A two-entry byte FIFO. When it is full and both a read and a write are requested, only the read happens. Reset clears it.
